editorial.headline: Aircraft Leasing Is Nationally Open, but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This operator-free aircraft, balloon and helicopter leasing activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Air-transport equipment can be rented in ways that look similar on the surface but are treated differently by the scope of this activity. This one is limited to the rental and operational leasing, without an option to buy, of air-transport equipment supplied without an operator. Aircraft, balloons and helicopters are expressly within the described equipment. The operating model is consequently equipment-only: the asset is provided without the person who operates it. Where an aircraft is rented with an operator, it falls outside this activity. That boundary defines what the registration is for.

The stated scale availability is wide. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, so the classification is not limited to one size of enterprise. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA and its maximum foreign ownership is 100%. Read plainly, the national record permits full foreign ownership; it does not state a lower foreign-share cap. This national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the activity at national level, the equipment-only scope and the 100% ceiling are the starting frame.

Bali changes the practical result decisively. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope. That places the activity within the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. The stated provincial rule blocks PMA registration for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity; it is island-wide and permanent. The record therefore treats this as a Bali risk-class block and flags PMA registration as blocked.

The contrast needs no softening. A national ceiling of 100% does not change the fact that this activity cannot be registered as PMA in Bali today. The block follows the permanent, island-wide moratorium triggered by the risk classification at the Besar scale, not a national foreign-ownership ceiling. The practical reading is therefore two-part: nationally TERBUKA up to 100%; in Bali, blocked for PMA. Staying inside the scope matters just as much: the activity is the operator-free rental or operational leasing of the listed air-transport equipment.
